There is plenty of laughter of all kinds in James Ijames’ astonishing play, The Most Spectacularly Lamentable Trial of Miz Martha Washington, now on stage at Steppenwolf Theatre.

Whitney White's multilayered direction absolutely sparkles, making full use of Clint Ramos' set, which contains a round platform on which Martha's bed can roll forward or back, as well as a rich field of blooming cotton that surrounds it.

Director Whitney White's bravura production features fearless performances by a cast that includes Sydney Charles, Carl Clemons-Hopkins, Celeste M. Cooper, Nikki Crawford, Cindy Gold, Victor Musoni and Donovan Session.
Ijames’s play, now finally making its long-postponed Steppenwolf premiere, isn’t about making nice with White Woman Tears.

cn.t: Critics praise Ijames' wildly entertaining fever dream that puts Martha Washington on trial for slavery, calling it a provocative, darkly comedic spectacle that's both uproarious and thought-provoking in its indictment of America's founding mythology.
